title: Cell-5 manual FS+HP tuning (XGBoost) — beating sweep R-Precision@1 by +24%

r_precision_at_k_methodology_note.definition: R-Precision@K = (1/Q) * sum_{q in Q} r_q / min(K, R_q), where Q is the set of days with R_q > 0 positives, R_q is the count of positives on day q, r_q is the count of positives in the top-K picks on day q. Macro-averaged across days, equal weight per day. Tie-break for sorting predictions: (p_calibrated desc, ticker asc) stable mergesort. See .claude/memories/project-r-precision-methodology.md.
r_precision_at_k_methodology_note.memo_body_uses: R-Precision@K (per-day fixed K, macro-averaged across days where R_q > 0).

headline: Manual XGBoost tuning (FS + response-curve + mix-and-match + eval-validation) beats sweep R-Precision@1 by +0.157 (+24% relative) on cell-5 (nasdaq100 +10%/50d/dd5%). Test R-p@1: sweep CatBoost 0.6714, agent loop XGBoost 0.5429, manual XGBoost 0.8286. The winning config is a 6-tree, depth-2 XGBoost model (<=24 leaves) with light regularization (lambda=1 default, alpha=0, gamma=0) + colsample_bytree=0.4 + eta=0.1 with early-stopping + FS to top-130 features by iter_0 importance. The agent loop's heavy regularization direction (mcw=10+gamma=1) was actively wrong on this anti-AUC strong-top-1 cell -- val_brier has a degenerate global minimum at the constant predictor, and the L1 tie-break selects toward it. The methodology codified here (rules 10-12 in the playbook) is general for anti-AUC + strong-top-1 cells.

anti_auc_anomaly.claude_md_rule: AUC in [0.45, 0.55] AND R-Precision@10 lift > 1.5x -> top-tail signal hidden by AUC -- investigate the prediction-extreme regime

fs.rank_basis: iter_0 XGBoost feature_importance (gain) on the full 279-feature set + cliff-cut FS pre-prune

methodology_stages.name: FS cliff cut
methodology_stages.outcome: Drop 89 features at importance < 0.01 (the natural cliff: 0 features in 0.001-0.01, 89 at exactly 0). Byte-identical model under colsample=1.0 (zero-importance features never selected). Establishes 190-feature working set.

methodology_stages.name: single-knob response curves
methodology_stages.outcome: Map val_brier response across 8 knobs. gamma + alpha curves descend monotonically to a degenerate sink at val=0.226 (the weighted-base-rate constant predictor) -- the val_brier 'winner' is the trivial model. max_depth has inverted-U at d=3. scale_pos_weight at 2.0. Other knobs mild.

methodology_stages.name: mix-and-match around non-degenerate winners
methodology_stages.outcome: Lean backbone (depth=2 + cs=0.4 + spw=2 + nest=50 + gamma=0) emerges as val R-p@1 leader at 0.530.

methodology_stages.name: eval-segment validation
methodology_stages.outcome: Eval reshuffles the val ordering dramatically. val R-p@1 rank-1 (lean) -> eval rank 6. eta=0.1 + ES emerges as eval rank 1 despite mediocre val. Val R-p@1 is unreliable on this cell.

methodology_stages.name: eta + early-stopping neighborhood probe
methodology_stages.outcome: eta=0.1 + ES30 is sweet spot. ES window invariant {20,30,40,50}. Removing scale_pos_weight (=1.0) helps eval R-p@1: best_iter drops to 3, eval R-p@1 -> 0.627.

methodology_stages.name: FS refinement
methodology_stages.outcome: FS sweep around top-130: top-130 + champ-spw -> eval R-p@1 = 0.7377 (the new champion). best_iter = 6.

methodology_stages.name: 1-shot TEST shootout
methodology_stages.outcome: Test confirms eval ranking for top 2. Manual winner test R-p@1 = 0.8286, +24% over sweep 0.6714. Manual loses to sweep at K=5/K=10 (K=1 specialized).

findings.F1_val_brier_degenerate_sink: val_brier has a global minimum at the weighted-base-rate constant predictor (val=0.226 for this cell). Any monotonically-shrinking reg knob (gamma, alpha) walks toward it. Optimizing val_brier alone selects the trivial model.
findings.F2_val_R_p_K_unreliable: Q_days x 1 pick/day is a tiny effective sample for val R-p@1. Configs ranked #1 by val R-p@1 landed at eval rank 6; configs ranked #10 landed at eval rank 2. Val R-p@K cannot be the iteration oracle on this cell.
findings.F3_eval_R_p_K_reliable: Eval R-p@1 rankings correlate with test R-p@1 rankings for the top contenders. Use eval R-p@K as the holdout oracle when val signals disagree.
findings.F4_tiny_models_win_top_1: 6 trees of depth 2 (<=24 leaves) beat sweep's CatBoost-default (1000 iters, depth 6, ~64,000 max leaves) by 24% on test R-p@1. Don't dismiss tiny configs whose val_brier is close to baseline -- that's exactly the 'smart prior + tiny corrections' shape that wins on anti-AUC cells.
findings.F5_loop_direction_wrong: Agent loop final (mcw=10 + gamma=1) test R-p@1 = 0.543 -- WORSE than baseline 0.343 only because baseline has cliff-cut FS that doesn't fix the wrong-direction reg. The loop's heavy reg pushes toward the degenerate sink; light reg + small model + aggressive FS goes the opposite direction.
findings.F6_K_1_specialization: The winner sweeps test R-p@1 (+24% vs sweep) but loses test R-p@5 (-7.5%) and test R-p@10 (-7.7%). The model is K=1-specialized -- ideal for top-pick portfolios; sweep would still win for broader top-K strategies.

infrastructure_notes.data_reuse: All batches reuse the same per-cell features parquet from the manual artifact dir (no rebuild after stage 1).
infrastructure_notes.fit_wall_clock: Each fit is 3-10s on hist+nj=8 (PR #107). Entire 8-batch methodology was ~15 min wall-clock end-to-end.

rules_added: Rule 10 - eval-as-oracle on anti-AUC + strong-top-1 cells
Rule 11 - FS -> response-curve -> mix-and-match -> eval-validation manual methodology
Rule 12 - tiny models can dominate big ones on top-1; don't dismiss configs whose val_brier is close to baseline
claude_md_added: val_brier has a degenerate global minimum at the constant predictor on anti-AUC cells -- don't ship the val_brier winner without scoring R-Precision@K too
Don't dismiss tiny models on top-1 metrics on anti-AUC cells
skill_md_added: Anti-AUC + strong-top-1 cell flag in pre-flight: when this triggers, opt into the manual-tuning track (rules 10-12) instead of running the standard loop
